job.title: Senior Customer Service Manager
job.description:
Senior Manager, Service and Experience


East Midlands, 3 to 4 days on site | c.£75,000


Lead service and customer experience for a technology-led service business, running a 35 seat operation that serves business accounts and individual consumers.


The operation is small enough to move quickly and busy enough that nothing sits still. Demand shifts week to week, business customers and consumers want different things from the same team, and the technology behind the service is moving faster than the processes built around it. This role owns how customers experience all of it, and where that experience goes next.


What you'll own

  • The experience strategy: where service goes over the next 2 years and the decisions that get it there
  • Experience projects end to end: diagnosing the journey, redesigning it, delivering the change, and proving what it did for customers and for the numbers
  • The commercial performance of the function: cost to serve, retention, and the case for every investment you ask for
  • Technology and data: the platforms the team works in, what the data is saying, and what changes as a result
  • Service standards across contracted business accounts and consumer customers, with the tension between the two handled well
  • A 35 seat operation: team leaders, structure and capability


You'll be the voice of the customer at senior level, working closely with commercial, technology and operations, and trusted to make the calls when demand, priorities and systems are all moving at once.


Our ideal applicant

  • A service leader: currently leading a customer service or experience operation in a mid-sized business, with both business and consumer customers
  • Has run experience projects from diagnosis through to delivery and can show the results
  • Commercially minded: reads a P&L, understands cost to serve, and knows what good service is worth to the business
  • Works in an agile way in the practical sense: tests, learns, changes course when the evidence says so
  • At home in a service environment where the technology is central to the product
  • As comfortable building the roadmap as sitting with the team listening to calls


The package

  • c.£75,000 base salary
  • 3 to 4 days on site in East Midlands, with flexibility around the rest
  • Great corporate benefits

job.title: Digital Transformation and Customer Experience
job.description:
Interim Digital Transformation Lead, Customer Social housing, North West | Initially 3 months | Start October


Lead the digital transformation of the customer function for a North West housing group, starting in October on an initial 3 month digital transformation project as an extension of the Customer directorate.


The organisation is in good health and has a way to go on digital. This role sets the roadmap direction and gets the first stages moving.


What you'll do

  • Establish where the organisation sits on digital today, with the evidence behind it
  • Build the route map: the areas that will make the biggest difference, in the order they should be tackled, with the case for each one
  • Deliver the first stages inside the 3 months, so tenants see something change
  • Hold the customer view and the technical view together across the whole of it
  • Hand over to the internal team, working with the transformation ownership already in place


Our ideal applicant

  • A customer leader. You have run a customer function, owned the numbers behind it, and been accountable for what customers experienced
  • Comes from a sector further along on digital than housing, and can pitch that experience to where this organisation actually is
  • Has been inside a core system, app or portal build, close enough to challenge how it was designed
  • Designs from the start for the customer who cannot or will not go online
  • Has worked to a regulator and knows what that does to the standard
  • Works comfortably inside an exec team and says what is going wrong


What's on offer

  • Initially 3 months, with scope to extend
  • Start October 2026
  • Day rate to agree, around £100,000 salary equivalent
  • North West, 3 days onsite

job.title: Head of Customer Service
job.description:
Head of Customer Service


Greater Manchester (office based, full time) · £95,000 + benefits


Run the customer service operation for a high-volume competitive consumer retailer. 80+ people across in-house teams and outsourced partners, and a wide range making up the customer base.


The contact profile is broad. Order and delivery questions at volume, returns and refunds, complaints that carry a regulated process and formal deadlines, and queries on products sold by partner brands. Volumes swing hard through peak trading, add all this into a very competitive sector and service has to be flawless.


There is change happening across the business. New technology, a customer function being redesigned, and work underway on how much of the operation sits with outsourced partners. This role plays a part in the delivery of all of it. What it is measured on is the day to day: how fast customers get an answer, how well the operation runs, what it costs, the culture in the teams, and what customers say afterwards.


What you'll own

  • Day to day performance of the contact centre across 80+ people: speed of answer, resolution, quality, cost to serve
  • What customers tell you, what it means, and getting the causes fixed with the teams that create them
  • The culture on the floor: the standard your managers hold, how people are coached, whether good people stay
  • The outsourced partner relationships: performance, quality, commercials, and a consistent experience whoever the customer reaches
  • Efficiency: forecasting and scheduling through peak, contact reduction, and the balance between automated and human channels
  • The structure underneath you and the capability of the managers in it


You'll report to the Customer Experience Director as their number 2. They hold the wider experience and commercial agenda. You hold and stabalise the operation, with the room to run it your way, and involvement in some of the change work wherever it touches service.


The first 12 months

Get hold of the operation and steady the contact types that are costing the business trust. Put measures in place that tell you the truth about performance week to week. Lift the standard of the management layer through investement into cross-training, performance management and upskilling all roles from complaints through to senior managers.


Our ideal applicant

  • A service leader who has run a contact centre of similar scale and challange: forecasting, scheduling, quality frameworks, and what moves the numbers week to week
  • Has managed outsourced partners on performance, quality and the commercial conversation
  • Comfortable with a mixed contact profile, transactional order queries at volume alongside complaints that carry a regulated process
  • Builds culture deliberately: coaches managers, holds a standard, and keeps good people in the building
  • Runs on numbers and can talk to cost to serve, contact rate and what poor service costs the business
  • Steady in a business that is changing around them, and clear on what service needs to stay solid while it does
  • A leader who has held consistency of role and lead service delivery through various sizes of teams is crucial for this role


The package

  • £95,000 base salary
  • Full time, office based in Greater Manchester
  • Benefits detail shared on application


All applications are handled confidentially by Stellify.

job.title: Recruitment Consultant
job.description:
Recruiter Liverpool, Royal Albert Dock. £28,000 to £32,000 plus commission, with full training.


We Are Stellify is one of the fastest growing recruitment businesses in Liverpool. We place the people who run and transform customer functions, and the name is already known to chief executives and customer leaders around the UK.


We're growing fast, and we're looking for a Recruitment Consultant to be part of it.

Joining a scale up means joining something still being built. It changes month to month, it invests where it's growing, and for an ambitious salesperson there's no better place to get good quickly.


The desk supports SaaS tech businesses on the hires that keep their customers engaged. Clients are UK wide and the market is busy. You'll place leadership roles across Customer Experience, Helpdesk, Account Management and Customer Success.


You'll work directly with our founder, 15 years in this industry and a top performer for most of them. The training behind this role is what makes it a fast track. You'll be in client conversations early, and you'll learn how to work with a client to build a role that has real impact. You'll get to know the talent in a market that keeps growing, and the depth of that insight is what sets you apart.


Apply if you want to be good at this quickly, and you like the idea of the business growing around you while you do it.


What we're looking for

Hard working. Tech savvy. Outgoing. Someone who sells a solution rather than reads a script.

Recruitment or sales experience helps. Neither is required. We'll teach you the tips and the tricks. What we can't teach is a natural ability to build a relationship and keep it.


What you get

Full training from someone who has done this at the top level. £28,000 to £32,000, plus commission. 30 days holiday including bank holidays. Health cash plan from your first day. High quality kit and some of the best AI powered technology in the market. Quarterly lunch clubs and a proper social calendar. Discounted parking at the Dock.


Office based at the Royal Albert Dock, with flexibility around home working and client meetings. The first year of this job is learned by overhearing it, which is why we want you in the office.

job.title: Director of CX Operations
job.description:
Customer Experience Director

Greater Manchester (office based, full time) · Senior leadership package, C£110,000 + Benefits

Lead the customer function for a large multi-brand retailer, at the point where the whole operation is being rebuilt around the customer and run as a commercial contributor rather than a cost to manage.

Retail customer functions carry more moving parts than most: high volumes, seasonal peaks, returns and refunds, and customers who compare and switch in seconds. This is a transformation post. The contact centre is moving off an outsourced model, new technology is coming in, and the function is being redesigned from the ground up. It suits a customer leader who wants the room to build, not a narrow slice of an operation that already runs itself.

What you'll own

  • The design of the customer operating model, and the commercial case for what the function becomes and where it sits
  • The move of the contact centre from an outsourced model, one of the largest and most complex decisions in the role
  • The technology agenda: choosing what comes in, and getting the business to adopt it and use the data properly
  • Service design across the moments that carry the most weight in retail, including returns, refunds, peak trading and the balance of automated and human channels
  • Retention and the commercial numbers behind loyalty and repeat purchase, and the plan to move them
  • Building and coaching the team, setting clear measures and lifting capability across managers and agents

You'll sit on the senior leadership team with direct access to the CEO, work closely with Trading, Operations, Marketing and Technology, and be trusted to make the calls that decide what this function becomes.

Our ideal applicant

  • A customer leader who has owned a customer function end to end in a high-volume, multi-channel retail or consumer business
  • Has led real transformation of a customer operating model, ideally including a move from outsourced delivery to in-house
  • Has brought in technology and knows the difference between buying it and getting a business to use it
  • Runs the function commercially, with retention and cost numbers you can talk to
  • Comfortable with the pace and complexity of retail, and drawn to building something rather than maintaining it

The package

  • Competitive senior leadership package, C:110,000 full details shared on application
  • Full time, office based in Greater Manchester

job.title: Customer Support & Insights Manager
job.description:
Customer Insight and Performance Manager


Liverpool (office based) | £40,000 to £44,000 including car allowance


Own performance, insight and regulatory compliance for a small, regulated property business where reporting goes all the way to Board. This role is the organisation's eyes: what's working, what's at risk, and what the data says should change.


The remit is broad for the size of business, and that's the appeal. You'll build the performance framework rather than inherit one, and your reporting will sit in front of Board and leadership every cycle.


What you'll own

  • The performance and insight framework: designing it, running it, and making it the way the business understands itself
  • Regulatory compliance and assurance: monitoring statutory and regulatory requirements, coordinating reporting for regulatory returns, internal reviews and external audits
  • Board reporting: papers, dashboards and exception reports that hold up to scrutiny
  • Customer complaints and feedback analysis, turned into recommendations that change how services run
  • Contractor and partner performance: KPIs, SLAs, and the meetings where accountability actually happens
  • Business systems and data improvement: better data quality, simpler workflows, and supporting new systems from testing through to training
  • Line management of a Compliance Officer, plus mentoring apprentices


Our ideal applicant

  • A customer-led performance leader: uses insight, complaints and service data to improve customers' experience, and can show where it worked
  • Strong on statutory and regulatory compliance, and confident being the person the organisation relies on to stay ahead of it
  • Skilled at data interrogation and analysis, and clearer still at explaining what the numbers mean to a Board
  • Comfortable challenging contractors and partners while keeping the relationship working


The package

  • £40,000 to £45,000, including car allowance
  • 35 hours, Monday to Friday, with flexi time
  • Office based in Liverpool
  • Pension with employer contribution
  • 25 days holiday plus bank holidays
